stem: Figure shows currents in a part of electrical circuit. Find the current \(X\)?
solution:
[Textbook misprint: two defects in this example, and the working below has been CORRECTED for the second. (1) The stem asks for "the current \(X\)", but no current labelled \(X\) appears anywhere in the figure — every branch is labelled \(I_1\) to \(I_7\), so the quantity asked for is undefined; the printed solution in fact finds \(I_3\), \(I_5\) and \(I_6\). (2) At junction C the book writes \(I_5 = I_3 + I_4\) and obtains \(I_5 = 16\) A, and hence \(I_6 = 7\) A. But in the figure the arrow on the \(I_4 = 2\) A branch points AWAY from C — drawn identically to the \(I_2 = 3\) A branch at junction B, which the same working correctly SUBTRACTS. Applying the junction law consistently with the figure gives \(I_3 = I_4 + I_5\), so \(I_5 = 14 - 2 = 12\) A and \(I_6 = 12 - 9 = 3\) A. The working below uses these corrected values.]

At junction B, current \(I_1\) is split into \(I_2\) and \(I_3\), therefore \(I_1 = I_2 + I_3\).
Substituting values we get \(17 = 3 + I_3\), so \(I_3 = 14\) A.
At junction C the branch current \(I_4\) leaves the junction, so \(I_3 = I_4 + I_5\), giving \(I_5 = 14 - 2 = 12\) A.
At junction D, \(I_5 = I_6 + I_7\), giving \(I_6 = 12 - 9 = 3\) A.

stem: Two batteries of 7 volt and 13 volt and internal resistances 1 ohm and 2 ohm respectively are connected in parallel with a resistance of 12 ohm. Find the current through each branch of the circuit and the potential difference across 12-ohm resistance.
solution:
Let the currents passing through the two batteries be \(I_1\) and \(I_2\).
Applying Kirchhoff second law to the loop AEFBA,
\(-12(I_1 + I_2) - 1 I_1 + 7 = 0\)
\(12(I_1 + I_2) + 1 I_1 = 7\) --- (1)
For the loop CEFDC
\(-12(I_1 + I_2) - 2 I_2 + 13 = 0\)
\(12(I_1 + I_2) + 2 I_2 = 13\) --- (2)
From (1) and (2), \(2 I_2 - I_1 = 13 - 7 = 6\)
\(I_1 = 2 I_2 - 6\)
Substituting \(I_1\) value in (2)
\(I_2 = \dfrac{85}{38} = 2.237\) A
\(I_1 = 2 I_2 - 6 = 2 \times \dfrac{85}{38} - 6 = -1.526\) A
\(I = I_1 + I_2 = -1.526 + 2.237 = 0.711\) A
Potential difference across the 12 \(\Omega\) resistance
\(V = IR = 0.711 \times 12 = 8.532\) V

stem: For the given network, find the current through 4 ohm and 3 ohm. Assume that the cells have negligible internal resistance.
solution:
[Textbook misprint: the last line is printed as \(I_3 = I_1 + I_2 = 2.12 - 0.5 = 1.625\) A. The displayed subtraction is inconsistent — \(2.12 - 0.5 = 1.62\) — because \(I_1 = 2.125\) A has been truncated to 2.12 in that one line. The stated final answer \(I_3 = 1.625\) A is correct and follows from \(2.125 - 0.5\). Preserved as printed.]

Applying Kirchhoff's first law:
At junction F, \(I_1 + I_2 = I_3\) --- (1)
Applying Kirchhoff second law,
(i) loop EFCDE, \(3 I_2 - 4 I_1 + 10 = 0\)
\(4 I_1 - 3 I_2 = 10\) --- (2)
(ii) loop FABCF, \(-4 I_3 - 3 I_2 + 5 = 0\)
\(4 I_3 + 3 I_2 = 5\) --- (3)
From Eq. (1) and Eq. (2)
\(4(I_3 - I_2) - 3 I_2 = 10\)
\(-3 I_2 + 4 I_3 - 4 I_2 = 10\)
\(4 I_3 - 7 I_2 = 10\) --- (4)
From Eq. (3) and Eq. (4)
\(10 I_2 = -5\)
\(I_2 = -0.5\) A
Negative sign indicates that \(I_2\) current flows from F to C.
From Eq. (2) \(4 I_1 - 3(-0.5) = 10\)
\(I_1 = 2.125\) A
\(\therefore I_3 = I_1 + I_2 = 2.12 - 0.5 = 1.625\) A

stem: At what value should the variable resistor Q be set in the circuit such that the bridge is balanced? If the source voltage is 30 V find the value of the output voltage across \(XY\), when the bridge is balanced.
solution:
[Textbook misprint: the line "Potential difference across AC \(= I_1 \times 24340 = 30\)" prints 24340, but the resistance of the arm ADC computed on the line immediately above is \(24347\ \Omega\), and the very next line correctly uses \(I_1 = 30/24347\). The 24340 is a typographical slip and the answer does not depend on it. Preserved as printed.]

When the bridge is balanced
\(P/Q = R/S\)
\(Q = PS/R\)
\(= \dfrac{1.36 \times 10^{3} \times 4.4 \times 10^{3}}{300} = 19946.66\ \Omega\)
Total resistance of the arm ADC \(= 19947 + 4400 = 24347\ \Omega\)
To find output voltage across \(XY\):
Potential difference across AC \(= I_1 \times 24340 = 30\)
\(I_1 = \dfrac{30}{24347}\) A
Potential difference across AD is \(V_{AD} = I_1 \times 19947 = (30 \times 19947)/24347 = 24.58\) V
\(I_2 = \dfrac{30}{1360 + 300} = \dfrac{30}{1660}\) A
Hence, potential difference across AB is
\(V_{AB} = I_2 \times 1360 = \dfrac{30}{1660} \times 1360 = 24.58\) V
\(V_{out} = V_D - V_B = V_{AB} - V_{AD} = 24.58 - 24.58 = 0\) V

stem: Two resistances 2 ohm and 3 ohm are connected across the two gaps of the metre bridge as shown in figure. Calculate the current through the cell when the bridge is balanced and the specific resistance of the material of the metre bridge wire. Given the resistance of the bridge wire is 1.49 ohm and its diameter is 0.12 cm.
solution:
When the bridge is balanced, the resistances 2 and 3 ohm are in series and the total resistance is 5 ohm.
Let \(R_1\) be the resistance of the wire \(= 1.49\ \Omega\), and \(R_2\) be the total resistance \((2+3) = 5\ \Omega\).
\(R_p = \dfrac{R_1 R_2}{R_1 + R_2} = \dfrac{1.49 \times 5}{1.49 + 5} = 1.15\ \Omega\)
The current through the cell
\(= \dfrac{\varepsilon}{R_p} = \dfrac{2}{1.15} = 1.739\) A
Specific resistance of the wire \(= \rho = \dfrac{R \pi r^{2}}{l}\)
\(l = 1\) m, \(r = \dfrac{0.12}{2} = 0.06\) cm, \(R = 1.49\ \Omega\)
\(\rho = \dfrac{R \pi r^{2}}{l} = \dfrac{1.49 \times 3.14 \times (0.06 \times 10^{-2})^{2}}{1}\)
\(= 1.686 \times 10^{-6}\ \Omega\) m \((\pi = 3.142)\)
